title: Handle-time bonus pilot and proposed network rollout at Corrigan Mutual Insurance

organization.size: approx. 2,300 staff; customer contact operation of about 460 front-line agents across four sites (Hartwell, Brookvale, Ashby Cross, Linden Park) plus a centralized 38-person tier-2 specialist desk

presentingRequest: Since we introduced an average-handle-time target with a monthly team bonus at our Hartwell site on 1 May, AHT there has dropped by 25%, and our customer satisfaction score hasn't moved - customers are getting the same service, faster. Finance estimates the bonus would save about $1.1M a year if we extend it to all four sites. We want to roll it out network-wide on 1 January 2027 and would like your help designing the rollout, the communication to agents, and the target levels for each site. - Denise Okafor, VP Customer Operations

evidence.text: 'Hartwell went from 9.6 minutes average handle time in the first four months of the year to 7.2 minutes from May to October. That's 25%. The bonus is $150 a month per agent when the team averages 7.5 minutes or less, so it's cheap. CSAT at Hartwell is 4.33 out of 5, same as before, and quality scores haven't moved either. Nobody has complained to me. If service had got worse, CSAT would show it. The other three sites are asking why Hartwell gets a bonus and they don't.'

'The team really bought into it. A lot of the improvement is the Fast Path coaching we ran in the spring and the new PolicyFind knowledge search - agents stopped putting people on hold to look things up. Transfers are up, sure, but that's because the HomeCyber add-on launched in May and those questions have to go to tier 2. My supervisors are drowning in agent-release alerts, which are mostly noise, so I've asked IT to switch them off for Hartwell.'

evidence.source: Workforce management monthly AHT report, Jan-Oct 2026, with metric definition
evidence.text: Average handle time (talk + hold + after-call work), minutes. Hartwell: Jan-Apr mean 9.6 (Jan 9.7, Feb 9.5, Mar 9.6, Apr 9.6); May 7.9, Jun 7.4, Jul 7.1, Aug 7.0, Sep 6.9, Oct 6.9; May-Oct mean 7.2. Brookvale, Ashby Cross and Linden Park combined: Jan-Apr mean 9.5 (range 9.3-9.7); May-Oct mean 9.4 (range 9.3-9.5). Metric definition (unchanged since 2023): AHT is calculated per agent call leg. A call transferred to the tier-2 desk counts as one handled call for the transferring agent, timed up to the moment of transfer; tier-2 handle time is reported in the tier-2 desk's own figures and not in the site's AHT. A call released by the agent counts as a handled call timed to the release.

evidence.source: L&D and IT change records (training log and release calendar)
evidence.text: Fast Path coaching programme: delivered to all agents at all four sites between 2026-03-02 and 2026-04-24 (completion: Hartwell 97%, other sites 95-98%). PolicyFind knowledge search: released to all four sites on 2026-04-20. HomeCyber add-on product: launched to all four sites on 2026-05-12; HomeCyber policy questions are routed to the tier-2 desk by design at every site. The AHT target and $150 monthly team bonus (team average <= 7.5 minutes) apply only to Hartwell, from 2026-05-01.

Post-call SMS survey, 1-5 scale. Hartwell: Jan-Apr mean 4.31, May-Oct mean 4.33. Other three sites: 4.29 and 4.30. Hartwell surveys sent per month: Jan-Apr mean 4,810; May-Oct mean 4,620, while Hartwell inbound calls handled rose from a Jan-Apr mean of 37,600 per month to a May-Oct mean of 41,000. Response rate steady at 21-23%. Other sites' surveys sent per month changed by less than 2%.

evidence.source: Survey vendor configuration export (eligibility rule, last modified 2024-02-12)
evidence.text: Survey eligibility: a call is eligible only if (a) its final disposition code is 'Resolved' and (b) it was not transferred. Calls with disposition 'Transferred', 'Released by agent', 'Abandoned' or 'Callback scheduled' are excluded. A random 15% of eligible calls are sent the SMS survey. The rule is identical at all four sites and has not been changed since 2024-02-12.

Share of handled calls transferred to tier 2 - Hartwell: Jan-Apr 11.2%, May-Oct 19.6% (rising from May, before the HomeCyber launch on 12 May; HomeCyber calls are 1.4% of Hartwell calls in May-Oct). Other sites: 11.0% and 12.3% (HomeCyber 1.3%). Agent-initiated releases (agent ends the call while the customer line is still open) - Hartwell: 0.5% then 2.3% of handled calls; other sites: 0.5% then 0.6%. Of Hartwell agent releases in May-Oct, 71% occurred between minute 6:00 and 7:30 of the call, against 18% in that window in Jan-Apr. No telephony hardware or software change at Hartwell in 2026.

evidence.source: Quality analyst, repeat-contact analysis (CRM customer-ID match, 2026-11-06)
evidence.text: 7-day repeat contact rate (same customer calls again within 7 days about the same policy). Hartwell: Jan-Apr 17.5%; May 21.9%, Jun 23.8%, Jul 25.6%, Aug 26.0%, Sep 25.1%, Oct 25.0%; May-Oct mean 24.6% (+41%). Other sites: 17.8% then 18.3%. Excluding the claims-status queue entirely, Hartwell rose from 16.9% to 23.1% (+37%). Among Hartwell repeat contacts in May-Oct, the prior call was transferred in 34% and agent-released in 9% (Jan-Apr: 19% and 2%).

evidence.source: Anonymous agent pulse survey, Hartwell free-text comments (October 2026, 64 respondents)
evidence.text: Selected verbatim comments: 'Anything that looks like it'll go past 6 minutes, you send it to tier 2. Everyone knows that.' 'If a call drops near 7 minutes, nobody asks questions.' 'I tell customers to ring back after they've found their documents instead of waiting on hold.' 'We are faster, but half my calls are people calling back.' 'The bonus is the team's, so you feel guilty if you take a long call.' 23 of 64 comments mention transfers, call-backs or 'the 7.5'.

'Transfers from Hartwell went from about 4,200 a month to over 8,000. We sampled 200 Hartwell transfers in September: 41% were questions any tier-1 agent is trained to answer - billing dates, address changes, simple coverage checks. Our average queue wait went from 2 minutes to 9 minutes and we've been on overtime since July. Transfers from the other sites look the same as last year apart from HomeCyber.'

evidence.source: Finance: bonus business case and Q3 cost report
evidence.text: Business case (2026-09-15): projected $1.1M annual saving if all sites achieve Hartwell's AHT reduction, calculated as tier-1 agent minutes saved per handled call x call volume, assuming volume unchanged. Q3 actuals for Hartwell: tier-1 handled calls +9% vs Jan-Apr run-rate; tier-2 overtime $46,000 (Q2: $3,000); total agent minutes (tier 1 + tier 2) per unique customer issue 11.4 in Jan-Apr vs 11.1 in Q3. Bonus paid at Hartwell May-Oct: $84,000 (paid for June-October; the May team average of 7.9 missed the target).

evidence.source: Customer complaints log, Hartwell-handled calls (formal written complaints)
evidence.text: Formal complaints mentioning being transferred, cut off or told to call back: Jan-Apr 2026 average 11 per month; May-Oct average 29 per month. Other sites: 10 and 11 per month. Example (2026-08-22): 'I was passed to a specialist, waited 12 minutes, and the specialist told me the first person could have answered it. Then I got cut off and had to start again.' Complaints are not linked to the CSAT survey and are not reported in the operations dashboard.

evidence.source: State weather service event record and claims intake data
evidence.text: A severe hailstorm hit the South-Central region, Hartwell's main service territory, on 2026-07-18. Hartwell claims-status call volume rose 31% in late July and August and returned to normal by the end of September. The other three sites serve regions with no comparable weather event in 2026.

evidence.source: HR attrition record and exit-interview log
evidence.text: Voluntary agent leavers, May-Oct 2026: Hartwell 9 of about 112 agents (same period 2025: 5); other sites 14 of about 348 (2025: 15). Hartwell's 6-month attrition has ranged from 3 to 8 leavers since 2022. In June 2026 a third-party outsourcer opened a 300-seat contact centre in Hartwell's town, advertising agent pay above Corrigan's rates; no comparable employer opened near the other sites. HR does not record leavers' next employer. Exit interviews were completed for 3 of the 9 Hartwell leavers: one cited 'pressure to keep calls short', one cited 'better pay elsewhere', one cited relocation. No exit interview recorded for the other 6.

evidence.source: Company-wide engagement pulse survey, 'I feel under excessive pressure at work' (agree = 5)
evidence.text: Hartwell: March 3.1, September 3.4. Other sites: March 3.2, September 3.4. On 2026-06-30 the company announced a back-office restructuring affecting all sites, which HR expected to raise stress scores everywhere.

evidence.source: Retention analytics: 90-day policy lapse by repeat-contact status, Hartwell customers
evidence.text: Customers with a 7-day repeat contact lapsed within 90 days at 4.8% (May-Oct 2026) vs 1.9% for customers with no repeat contact. Same comparison for May-Oct 2025, before the bonus: 4.5% vs 1.8%. Analyst note: repeat callers are disproportionately customers with disputed claims or premium-increase queries; an 8% premium increase took effect company-wide on 2026-07-01. Overall Hartwell 90-day lapse: 2.1% (Q2) and 2.6% (Q3); other sites 2.0% and 2.4%.

evidence.source: IT service request and alert design note
evidence.text: Real-time agent-release alert: notifies the on-floor supervisor within 30 seconds whenever an agent ends a call while the customer line is open. Design note (2023): 'the only intraday control on dropped and agent-ended calls; daily reports are reviewed weekly'. Service request SR-48812 from the Hartwell site manager (2026-10-27): 'Please disable agent-release alerts for Hartwell - alert volume has quadrupled since May and supervisors are spending too much time on them.' Status: pending approval by the VP Customer Operations.

hypotheses.text: The Hartwell AHT reduction reflects genuine efficiency gains, with customers receiving the same quality of service in less time.

Hartwell agents are reaching the AHT target partly by transferring calls they could resolve, ending calls early and asking customers to call back, which shifts unresolved work into repeat contacts and the tier-2 queue.
The stable Hartwell CSAT score is partly a measurement artifact, because the survey is never sent for transferred or agent-released calls, which are the outcomes that have increased.
The rise in Hartwell's 7-day repeat contacts is mainly explained by the July hailstorm and the resulting claims-status calls.
The AHT target and bonus are increasing voluntary agent attrition at Hartwell.

edges.from: AHT target and team bonus at Hartwell (from 2026-05-01)
AHT target and team bonus at Hartwell (from 2026-05-01)
edges.to: Increase in Hartwell transfers to tier 2 and agent-initiated call releases

edges.from: PolicyFind knowledge search and Fast Path coaching
edges.to: Fall in Hartwell reported AHT from 9.6 to 7.2 minutes
Customer lapsing their policy within 90 days

actions.text: Roll out the AHT target and $150 monthly team bonus to Brookvale, Ashby Cross and Linden Park on 2027-01-01 as planned, with site-specific AHT targets.

Halt the network rollout; redesign the Hartwell incentive so that any payout is gated on 7-day repeat contact, transfer and agent-release rates at or below their pre-pilot levels; and change survey eligibility so transferred and agent-released calls are also surveyed.
Give Hartwell agents a 6% base-pay increase to stem attrition caused by bonus pressure.
Approve service request SR-48812 and switch off the real-time agent-release alert at Hartwell to reduce supervisor workload.

Workforce management forecast of call volume for 2027
